notes.text: Re-check normalization for psi(x)=A on [0,4] next time by having the learner write integral of |A|^2 equals 1 to see why A is 1/2 not 0.25.
Build on the correct |3+4i|^2 calculation to reteach the missed normalization step that the constant A must be squared before integrating.
Use the correct |psi(x)|^2 dx probability idea to frame normalization as total probability equals 1 when revisiting the [0,4] problem.
Next time build on their correct recall of [x,p]=i hbar and shared eigenstates to derive uncertainty as intrinsic non-commutation, explicitly contrasting it with the photon-kick story they gave.
Re-teach the Gaussian wavepacket narrowing by having them explain momentum broadening via intrinsic Fourier spread, confronting their 'more precise measurement disturbs it more' explanation.
Use their correct Delta-p calculation to reconnect the formula to commutators and state-spread, checking they can apply it without invoking disturbance.
Have the learner compare vibrational spacing hbar-omega to room-temperature kT to re-check why the ground state dominates.
Build on correct lowering action and commutator to practice evaluating number-operator and energy expectations in excited states.
Re-ask for the norm argument behind a|0>=0 to consolidate the correct ladder-termination reasoning.

links.why: Learner justified that a|0> must vanish by appealing to non-negative energy.

notes.text: Build on correctly recalled 2 Sz outcomes and 1/2 probability for x-measurement from z-up to teach general spin-1/2 rotation probabilities next time.

Re-teach why second-order theory lowers the ground state from scratch next time, building on the correctly recalled first-order shift, since the analyze question was left unanswered even after the solution was shown.
Confront the disturbance explanation for x-z incompatibility by contrasting measurement disturbance with intrinsic indeterminacy using commutators and re-check with a new transfer example.
Have the learner compute <E> for the 0-epsilon two-level system using Z=4/3 and the -d ln Z/d beta rule to consolidate partition-function application.
Ask the learner to predict what happens to average energy when kT is no longer large versus level spacing to extend the correct equipartition condition.
Re-check recall of the e^{-E/kT} Boltzmann weight in a three-level calculation before introducing new statistical-mechanics material.
Confront the oil-and-water answer next time by asking the learner to account for water and energy changes so total entropy is seen to rise despite local ordering.
Build on the correct recall of S = k ln Ω and correct ΔS calculation next time by having the learner compute entropy changes for other Ω ratios.
Build on the correct F = -kT ln Z recall and partial entropy-matters explanation next time by deriving F = E - TS minimization explicitly at fixed T and V.

links.why: Learner explained F-minimization by appealing to entropy mattering at finite T.

notes.text: Re-teach Bose-Einstein divergence as E-mu approaches 0 by contrasting it with the correctly recalled Fermi-Dirac cap at 1 from Pauli exclusion.
Confront the 3kT/2-per-electron idea next time by reusing the learner's own Pauli-exclusion reasoning to show only states near mu can be thermally excited.
Build on the correct vibrational freeze-out explanation to teach electronic heat capacity as an analogous freeze-out where kT is far below the Fermi energy.

links.why: Learner explained suppressed metal electronic heat capacity with classical 3kT/2 per electron.
Learner explained low-temperature heat-capacity drop by mode freeze-out when kT falls below hbar omega.
